reports.title: Kayleigh Melhuish: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: We have carefully considered the potential for implementing changes to SystmOne to include a tick-box to confirm the review of the care plan and support actions.
promises.summary: Implement tick-box in SystmOne to confirm care plan review

promises.quote: We have recruited Neurodiversity Support Managers (NSMs) across the prison estate to ensure that support for neurodiverse prisoners is consistent across all education, skills and work opportunities as well as the wider prison. One of the main responsibilities of the NSMs is to provide training and support for other prison staff to help them better understand and support those with neurodivergent needs within the prison.
promises.summary: Recruit NSMs to train staff on neurodiversity support

concerns.quote: training issues in relation to the following areas for new and existing staff: Neurodiversity, I am told 75% of women in prison have mental health or neurodiverse issues, this training is not mandatory; ACCT, there was little understanding of the requirement to complete or review the care plan and support actions at every ACCT review not just the planned reviews; Little or no understanding of when constant supervision can be used and how is it used; Healthcare (AWP and PPG): training issues arose
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory neurodiversity and ACCT training leading to insufficient supervision and care plan compliance

reports.title: Rickie Poon: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: the ACCT process was not managed and implemented properly, e.g. supervising officers did not consistently acquaint themselves with case notes or history when completing reviews; record keeping was inadequate; agreed actions were not consistently implemented; and ACCT reviews lacked structure and consistency
there were gaps in training and knowledge, e.g. ACCT training had expired and prison staff overly relied on Rickie's presentation
the ACCT was closed too soon
I sent PFD reports to PPG's earlier incarnation, Care UK, and/or HMP Pentonville about the nature of attempts at resuscitation in respect of the following deceased
concerns.hazard: lack of follow‑up on previous resuscitation reports

links.explanation: Both reports identify shortcomings in ACCT-related training and knowledge among prison staff. The earlier report cites a lack of understanding of ACCT review requirements, while the later report notes expired ACCT training and over-reliance on a single presentation.
